newsitem.title: USA: N.J. group picks MFS over Lockheed for toll deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. group picks MFS over Lockheed for toll deal.

text.p: A consortium of New Jersey transportation officials Tuesday recommended that the state award a $500 million electronic toll collection contract to MFS Network Technologies of Moorestown, N.J.
MFS beat out Lockheed Martin IMS for the key endorsement from the Consortium for the Implementation of a Regional Electronic Toll Collection System.
Lockheed, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lockheed Martin Corp, was the only other company vying for what state officials said was the largest electronic toll collection contract in the nation.

Edward Gross, acting executive director of the state's Turnpike Authority, said in an interview that the recommendation is almost certain to be accepted when the agency votes next month to formally award the contract.
Prior to that vote, the boards of each the state's five major transportation agencies are expected to vote to authorize the Turnpike Authority to make the final award, Gross said.

The competition created controversy this month when the state's transportation commissioner, Frank Wilson, disclosed he had had job interviews with firms interested in the contract. Lockheed claimed that skewed the selection process, but a review by the Turnpike Authority said Wilson never influenced the selection.
Lockheed said it would issue a statement on the consortium's recommendation late Tuesday.
